content.user_title: Draft Employment Documents with Adaptable Templates
content.value_statement: Employment documents require consistent terms and careful customization. This skill provides adaptable templates, checklists, and drafting guidance for offers, agreements, and handbook policies.
actual_capabilities: Drafts customizable employment offer letters with role, compensation, benefits, contingencies, and acceptance terms.
Creates employment agreement sections covering duties, term, compensation, confidentiality, intellectual property, termination, and general provisions.
Produces employee handbook sections for equal opportunity, harassment, attendance, leave, conduct, technology, and social media.
Prompts users to confirm jurisdiction, employment type, required clauses, and document-specific details.
Provides drafting checklists and review practices for consistent employment documentation.
limitations: The templates provide general information and do not replace advice from qualified legal counsel.
Examples emphasize United States concepts and may not fit other jurisdictions.
The skill does not verify current laws, enforceability, or company-specific compliance requirements.
Every placeholder and optional clause requires accurate user input and professional review.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Candidate Offer
use_cases.description: Create a tailored offer letter with role details, compensation, benefits, contingencies, and an acceptance section.

use_cases.title: Structure an Employment Agreement
use_cases.description: Build a review-ready agreement outline for a new employee using supplied business terms and jurisdiction details.

use_cases.title: Standardize Handbook Policies
use_cases.description: Draft consistent workplace policy sections for onboarding materials and internal review.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Basic Offer Letter
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft an offer letter for [role] at [company]. Include [salary], [start date], [location], [employment type], and [benefits]. Mark missing details.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs a structured first draft from basic hiring terms.

prompt_templates.title: Create an Employment Agreement
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft an employment agreement for [jurisdiction] and [employment type]. Cover duties, compensation, confidentiality, intellectual property, termination, and dispute resolution. Flag counsel-review items.
prompt_templates.scenario: A company needs a comprehensive agreement outline for legal review.

prompt_templates.title: Build Handbook Policies
prompt_templates.prompt: Create handbook sections for [company] in [jurisdiction]. Include equal opportunity, harassment reporting, attendance, leave, conduct, technology, and social media policies.
prompt_templates.scenario: A people operations team is standardizing workplace policies.

prompt_templates.title: Review and Reconcile Documents
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare this offer letter, employment agreement, and handbook excerpt. Identify conflicting terms, missing placeholders, ambiguous language, and jurisdiction-sensitive clauses. Propose consistent revisions.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced user needs a cross-document consistency review before counsel approval.

output_examples.input: Draft an offer letter for a remote full-time product designer with a June start date and annual bonus eligibility.
output_examples.output: A structured offer letter covering position details, remote location, compensation placeholders, bonus eligibility, benefits, contingencies, at-will language, and acceptance signatures.

output_examples.input: Create an employee handbook section for reporting harassment and protecting employees from retaliation.
output_examples.output: A policy section defining prohibited conduct, listing reporting channels, describing prompt investigations, protecting confidentiality where possible, and prohibiting retaliation.

output_examples.input: Review an employment agreement for missing information before legal review.
output: Complete the governing-law and work-location fields.
Confirm whether employment is at-will or fixed-term.
Define bonus criteria and severance conditions.
Ask counsel to review restrictive covenants and intellectual property terms.

best_practices: Provide the jurisdiction, employment classification, work location, compensation, benefits, and required company policies.
Replace every placeholder and reconcile terms across the offer, agreement, and handbook.
Have qualified counsel review the final document before signature or distribution.
anti_patterns: Do not use a generic template without adapting it to applicable law and company practices.
Do not combine at-will and fixed-term language without resolving the conflict.
Do not present generated text as approved legal advice or guaranteed compliance.

faq.question: Does this skill provide legal advice?
faq.answer: No. It provides general templates and drafting guidance that require review by qualified legal counsel.

faq.question: Which documents can it draft?
faq.answer: It supports offer letters, employment agreements, handbook sections, and common workplace policies.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide jurisdiction, role, classification, work location, compensation, benefits, start date, termination terms, and required clauses.

faq.question: Can it create jurisdiction-specific clauses?
faq.answer: It can adapt wording from supplied requirements, but it does not verify local law or enforceability.

faq.question: Can it review an existing document?
faq.answer: Yes. It can identify missing placeholders, inconsistent terms, ambiguous language, and clauses that need professional review.

faq.question: Does it handle signatures or document storage?
faq.answer: No. It produces text only and does not collect signatures, file documents, or manage employee records.
